references.text: The parallel passage in Matthew where the disciples could not cast out the demon: "I brought him to your disciples, but they could not heal him."
The parallel passage in Mark where the father tells Jesus that he asked the disciples to cast out the spirit, but they were unable to do it.
Jesus explains privately to the disciples that this kind can only be driven out by prayer, which clarifies why they were unable to succeed.
The disciples ask Jesus why they could not drive out the demon, and Jesus answers that it was because of their little faith.
Jesus had previously given the twelve power and authority over all evil spirits, making it striking that they still could not cast out this demon.
The seventy returned with joy and said that even the evil spirits were subject to them in Jesus' name—a contrast to the disciples' inability in this case.
Jesus sent out the twelve and gave them authority over unclean spirits, emphasizing that they normally had been granted this power.
The story of the sons of Sceva who tried to cast out evil spirits without genuine spiritual authority—another example of failed exorcism.
